name: Portugal
summary: A spouse, children and ascendants are guaranteed a legitimate share, between a half and two thirds of the estate. A foreign resident can choose the law of their nationality (EU Succession Regulation art. 22). Portugal has no general trust law, and its foundations are for social-interest purposes.
reserved_share: Compulsory heirs are the spouse, descendants and ascendants (legítima, Civil Code arts. 2156-2161). Per e-Justice: spouse alone 1/2; one child alone 1/2, two or more 2/3; spouse with children 2/3; spouse with ascendants 2/3. The available quota (quota disponível) is the remainder.
foreign_law_note: EU Succession Regulation: the law of the last habitual residence applies by default (art. 21), but a resident foreign national may choose the law of their nationality (art. 22).
trust_note: Portugal did not sign the 1985 Hague Trusts Convention (not in the HCCH table). There is no domestic trust, except an offshore trust regime in the Madeira free zone (Decree-Law 352-A/88) for non-resident parties that cannot hold Portuguese real estate. Foundations (Framework Law 24/2012) are non-profit and serve a social-interest purpose.
open_questions: Article numbers on the e-Justice page (2139, 2142, 2144) differ from those commonly cited (2156-2161); fractions are from the page and should be checked against the Civil Code.
Current status of the Madeira trust regime (Decree-Law 352-A/88) was not confirmed.
Foundation purpose restriction taken from a Wikipedia-level summary, not Law 24/2012.
